text.content:
The Dark Medieval lacks modern medicine, so mortal wound recovery, disease, and poison behave very differently than in a modern chronicle. Vampire health-level tracking, wound penalties, and damage types (bashing/lethal/aggravated) are unchanged from the standard rules.

Mortal Healing Times

Each health level must be healed individually; a mortal Incapacitated by bashing damage must rest one week to reach Wounded and a further three days to reach Bruised, for example.

Health LevelBashingLethal
BruisedOne hour/levelOne day/level
WoundedOne day/levelOne week/level
IncapacitatedOne weekOne month
Mortally Wounded—Two months (at least)

Bashing damage heals with time alone, though medical attention can speed it. Lethal damage can turn septic: a character with lethal damage to the Bruised level or worse who receives no medical attention automatically loses an additional health level each day to infection and blood loss. Once a character above Wounded receives initial treatment, no further care is required. Incapacitated characters need constant care and are usually delirious or unconscious.

When a character attempts to heal a lethal health level at the end of the appropriate recovery time, she must win a Static Physical Challenge with a difficulty equal to her current number of marked-off wound levels. A win heals the level; a tie means no change and the recovery period must be repeated; a loss requires an additional Simple Test, and losing that as well costs an additional lethal wound (possibly causing death if it drops her below Incapacitated).

Disease

Vampires are largely immune to disease's direct effects but can act as vectors, infecting victims through the Kiss until the tainted vitae is purged. A mortal fed upon by an infected vampire must win a Static Physical Challenge (difficulty five, increasing by one each subsequent feeding from that vampire) to avoid infection.

  • Dysentery (the flux): Mortals lose Physical Traits over time and count as two Blood Traits lower than normal; no direct effect on Cainites, who can still transmit it via the Kiss.
  • Ergotism: Mortals may lose limbs to gangrene; a vampire who drinks ergot-tainted blood feels pins-and-needles in his limbs until the blood is purged.
  • Idropesie (dropsy): No effect on Cainites, but an afflicted vessel has two fewer Blood Traits than a healthy mortal.
  • Leprosy: Afflicted mortals don't notice damage until Wounded, and bashing wounds can turn lethal if left unattended; healing times double. Cainites are immune but can carry it.
  • Plague: Cainites are immune to bubonic and pneumonic plague (but can transmit them) and susceptible only to septicemic plague, which causes them to vomit one to three Blood Traits per turn (win a Simple Test = one turn, tie = two, loss = three) and requires a Static Physical Challenge (difficulty six) to keep fed blood down each time.
  • Syphilis: An infected vampire suffers one level of bashing damage at the start of each game session.
  • Tuberculosis (consumption): No effect on Cainites, but reduces an afflicted vessel's blood capacity by two Traits.
  • @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.derangements.JournalEntry.754855e1096f4bc8]{Saint Vitus's Dance}: A nervous disorder (modern Sydenham's chorea) transmissible to Cainites via infected blood, causing involuntary spasms. The afflicted character is one to three Traits down in some or all challenges, at the Narrator's discretion, until the affliction runs its course (days to weeks, sometimes recurring after months or years).

Purging Infected Vitae

Purging tainted blood follows the same process as purging any unwanted vitae: normal expenditure works until only five Blood Traits remain, then each of the final five requires spending a Willpower Trait and winning a Self-Control/Instinct Test (difficulty three Traits, four for the last two) to expel without frenzying. The difficulty is reduced by one per relevant Discipline the character holds (Vicissitude, Quietus, or the Thaumaturgy path Rego Vitae), to a minimum of one. Newly consumed vitae becomes infected as well until the vampire's system is fully purged.

Drugs and Poisons

  • Alcohol: For every two drinks consumed by the vessel, the feeding vampire gains the Negative Traits Clumsy and Oblivious, fading at one Negative Trait per hour or sooner.
  • Bloodroot (Sanguinaria): One of the few poisons directly harmful to Cainites — three aggravated health levels if consumed via blood, or two aggravated levels (plus weapon damage) if used as a contact poison, turning vitae to black ash.
  • Food Poisoning (Salmonella): Causes one level of bashing damage per Blood Trait consumed by the feeding vampire and makes her reluctant to keep drinking until purged.
  • Hashish: A vampire drinking hashish-tainted blood gains Oblivious and finds frenzy resistance one Trait easier, for about an hour.
  • Hallucinogens (henbane, deadly nightshade, etc.): Leave the vampire one to three Traits down in all challenges, plus effects similar to Fascination of the Soul, for several hours or the rest of the session.
  • Painkillers (hemlock, mandrake, monkshood): Reduce wound penalties by one health-level category (Bruised becomes unpenalized, Wounded takes Bruised penalties, etc.) for the same duration as hallucinogens.
  • Poison (arsenic, strychnine, cyanide, or large doses of the above): Leaves a Cainite one to three Traits down in all challenges and inflicts one to three levels of lethal damage; poison cannot kill or torpor a vampire outright, only incapacitate until purged and healed.

vtmlarp.source: Faith and Fire (Dark Ages Vampire), Chapter Five: Rules, Systems and Drama
